heuristics.statement: For one group, the chaining value CV1 = F_38(IV, M0) of a first block M0 built from two fresh uniform random words behaves as a uniform 256-bit value as far as the events of ONE fixed variant are concerned: for each A0 the table index (Y, Z0) is uniform (a bucket holds |R_j| 2^-27 entries in expectation), W7 is uniform and independent of (W0, W1) (an entry is a W7 pass with probability p2 = |F7| / 2^32 = 2^-3.90197), the first row-17 test passes with probability 2^-10 given a W7 pass, and the second-block words that realise a success have the distribution of proof.md Section 6.2 and Lemma 4. Groups use fresh coins and are independent. A statement about one first block and one variant at a time; nothing is assumed about two variants of one group (H5).
heuristics.scope: The three expected work counters (hence the caps and N_G), the per-variant success probability p2 q3 (hence the success bound). Not the validity of any output: every output is a verified collision (Lemma 7, Section 5.4).
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured by us on real chaining values (compression of uniform-looking first blocks by the real 38-step function, true buckets by exhaustive search, reference outcomes; proof.md Section 6.3): 12 real first blocks x 256 A0 (3,072 true buckets): entries 0.991 and W7 passes 0.99 times the H1 expectations, 1 first row-17 test passed (1.1 expected), 0 successes; 6 more chaining values: 1.037 and 0.92; The lemmas of Section 4 make the rest exact. The organizer experiment vt-ram-r38 runs the counted program on organizer-seeded first blocks and compares its table index, W7 decisions and W17 with the reference (a code-consistency check; the returned-pair count is a witness frequency of mismatch-free trials, not an inference). The caps use per-counter Chebyshev margins (2^-16, 2^-14, 2^-7, 2^-5) above the expectations over N_G = 2^66.5340 independent groups (Section 6.4).
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem. The measured events have probability between 2^-27 and 2^-41 per variant, not 2^-68. Only the first block varies between groups. Joint events of two variants on one real chaining value are the premise of H5.

heuristics.statement: The average of q3(v) = Pr[rows 16..37 hold | W7 in F7] over the variants the program examines (uniform on the union of the 256 sets R_j) and over uniform chaining values is at least q3_model = 2^-101.10 (this filing; the base aed05522 used 2^-101.35). Rows 16..22 have the same probability for every valid variant (Lemma 4, exact); only the tail (rows 23..37, through W8, W9, W10 of the variant) is averaged.
heuristics.scope: The expected number of successes per group S_model = SR p2 q3_model = 2^-67.52135, hence N_G, the success bound and the whole attack term of the ledger.
heuristics.extrapolation: Six Monte-Carlo studies with two estimators. This filing (proof.md Appendix E.2, from-scratch estimator q3.c, no code shared with smc.c): S1 (32 runs, seeds 1001..1032) mean 2^-100.99189, one-sided 99% bound 2^-101.03905; S2 (32 runs, seeds 2001..2032) mean 2^-100.99160, bound 2^-101.03081; pooled 2^-100.99174 / 2^-101.02120; 63,762 tail successes, each rebuilt into a verified 38-step semi-free-start collision (0 failed rebuilds); stage factors -27.00, -17.00, -13.01, -14.99, -6.00, -7.00, -1.00, -15.01. The estimator recomputes the A2 list (768), G (32 words) and |F7| = 287,309,824 exhaustively, draws variants uniformly from the union of the R_j by rejection (acceptance 0.00181, matching mean |R_j| / (768 x 2^29)), and tests every parsed cell and condition (the published pair satisfies all of them). Base studies (aed05522, preregistered, smc.c): R1-R4 means 2^-100.99875, 2^-101.00020, 2^-100.99986, 2^-100.99841, 99% bounds 2^-101.00146, 2^-101.00195, 2^-101.00265, 2^-101.00018. q3_model = 2^-101.10 is 0.061 bit below the lowest of the six bounds (2^-101.03905); it was chosen after the studies (not preregistered). With delta = 1/25, q3_model 2^-101.35 (the base value) would give 70.82120; 2^-101.5: 70.87779; 2^-102: 71.09360 (Appendix E.4). Organizer-executed: vt-q3-smc-r38 (unchanged) runs a reduced replica of the base estimator with rebuilt, verified pairs; its pass rule is a mean of 20 replicates >= 2^-101.35, so no organizer-run evidence reaches 2^-101.10. The paper (ePrint 2026/1120, Sect. 3.1) counts 102 conditions on rows 16..37; the measured probability of the tested event is 2^-101.0.
heuristics.limitations: Monte-Carlo estimates relying on the central limit theorem; q3 itself (about 2^-101) cannot be observed at full scale, so H2 is an evidence-supported heuristic premise, not a theorem. All six studies are participant-run; the new estimator is independent code but parses the same transcription of Section 3 (and the same W25 reading), so it is not independent data. The margin of q3_model below the lowest 99% bound is 0.061 bit and was chosen after seeing the data. Rests on H1 for the distribution of the second-block words. The reading W25[4] = W25[6] of the printed condition (the published pair fails the printed W25[4] = W25[9]) enters q3 only.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5 the online program is charged by its counted primitives: the model is a 256-bit word RAM whose primitives include 256-bit load and store, and memory is a reported metric with no scalar contribution. A load from any address costs one operation whatever the memory size; the memory used (2^80.42 bytes) is reported. Every table word is written by the counted preprocessing of proof.md Section 5.1 (zero initialisation included; the whole preprocessing is 2^66.9387 units).
heuristics.scope: The online cost per (chaining value, A0): one header load and a scan of the sentinel-terminated bucket (6 operations per entry) instead of a search over 2^29.5 variants.
heuristics.extrapolation: Follows the text of the cost model collision-frontier-v5: memory_scoring is "Required and reviewed as a metric only; no scalar contribution and no tie-break" and memory_includes lists code, nonuniform advice, precomputed data, messages, working state, tables and randomness retained in memory (all of which are in the reported figure); the same pricing is used by the public package 0ae69bcb (rank 1 on this track, passed review), which also reports the sensitivity if tables were not unit cost. The online and table-construction costs are counted by the interpreter of experiments/vt38.py and the preprocessing bodies of Appendix B.3; every table word of every table is written by the charged P6 passes (the zero pass over the 2^64 headers of every A0 costs 2^73.1 operations by itself).
heuristics.limitations: The tables are far beyond physical memory; without unit-cost table access the claim does not hold. Finding the buckets through the inverse of s0(u) - u instead of tables costs much more (Section 7 of 0ae69bcb: about 80.7).

heuristics.statement: The total computation spent to obtain the published 38-step characteristic of [LZLLQZ26] (IACR ePrint 2026/1120, Table 3: failed and repeated searches and tool development included) is at most A_C = 2^70 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The allowance part of the ledger: A_C is 60.1% of T (2^70 of 2^70.73486) and the largest single term.
heuristics.extrapolation: [LZLLQZ26] (IACR ePrint 2026/1120) uses the open-source CPU SAT/SMT automated characteristic-search tool of [LLW24a] (EUROCRYPT 2024) in the two-block framework of [LLWS26] (IACR ePrint 2026/1080), so GPU lane throughput does not apply to a CPU SAT/SMT solver and the operative hardware ceiling is the CPU branch of the bound chain: 10^5 CPU cores for 10 years at 10^10 word operations per second is 3.2 x 10^23 operations = 2^66.6 units at C = 2728; A_C = 2^70 is 10.3 times that ceiling. Cross-check against an organizer-accepted measured benchmark: the promoted filing 6eeefb64 (sha256-r32) priced a complete measured re-run of the predecessor 35-step characteristic search with the same [LLW24a] tool at 593,858 solver CPU-seconds over 59 solver calls; at its calibrated price of 2^32.796 primitive operations per solver CPU-second (2^21.383 units at C = 2728) and a 32-fold blind-rediscovery factor (as in 0ae69bcb) that is 2^45.6 units; A_C = 2^70 is 2^24.4 times that measured re-run (about 14 million CPU-years, roughly 2,000 times a SHAttered-scale computation). Furthermore, every cell and two-bit condition of the published 38-step characteristic is verified directly by the organizer-executed package (experiments/vt38.py selftest items 1-3 and vt-q3-smc-r38 across 20 organizer-seeded replicates). The same A_C = 2^70 allowance is charged by the accepted filings 0ae69bcb, 63028099, 37742a53 and 012400ff on this track. A_C = 2^72 gives 72.22165, 2^74 gives 74.05869, 2^76 gives 76.01490 (this filing, Appendix E.4). The paper reports the Step-1 cost (about 2^38.3) but no time or hardware for the characteristic search.
heuristics.limitations: A_C is a conservative upper bound above the operative CPU-hardware ceiling for the [LLW24a] SAT/SMT solver and 2^24.4 times the measured predecessor search re-run, rather than a direct timing log of the authors' unpublished 38-step search. The effect of a larger A_C is priced in Section 7 (A_C = 2^72, 2^74, 2^76). A GPU branch of the bound chain (10^4 GPUs, 10 years: 2^73.3, retained only for reference as in 0ae69bcb and 63028099) is not the operative branch because the solver is a CPU SAT/SMT tool.

heuristics.statement: The total computation spent to obtain the Step-1 solution (the published semi-free-start pair of Table 5 and its dense part S*) is at most A_S = 2^60 target compressions. The variants (A0, A1, A2) of S* needed by this package are not solved for: they are enumerated by the charged preprocessing P5.
heuristics.scope: The allowance part of the ledger (2^60 of the allowances; A_S and DEV together are 0.12% of T).
heuristics.extrapolation: [LZLLQZ26] reports about 2^38.3 compression-equivalent calls for the 38-step Step-1 solve (and 2^41.3 for 37 steps); A_S = 2^60 is 2^21.7 times the published Step-1 figure (a margin of more than three million-fold; the accepted r37 filings 087a18c4, 1f12a09a, 7319bba9 and 8de337d5 charge A_S = 2^50, and A_S = DEV = 2^50 here would give 70.73317). Moreover, the published semi-free-start pair (Table 5) and its dense part S* are verified directly by experiments/vt38.py (selftest item 1), and the organizer-executed experiment vt-q3-smc-r38 constructs and verifies dozens of fresh 38-step semi-free-start collisions from variant dense parts in a few seconds inside the organizer sandbox (21 returned verified pairs per organizer run, 0 failed rebuilds), directly demonstrating that completing a variant dense part to a verified 38-step semi-free-start collision costs well below 2^35 units. The same A_S = 2^60 allowance is accepted in 37742a53 and 012400ff on this track.
heuristics.limitations: The original SAT/SMT search for the base dense part S* was performed by the paper's authors and is bounded by 2^21.7 times their reported figure rather than re-solved from scratch in the organizer sandbox (which instead verifies S* and constructs fresh 38-step semi-free-start pairs from its variants in vt-q3-smc-r38). Raising A_S to 2^70 (the allowance of 0ae69bcb and 63028099) together with DEV = 2^64 gives 71.42111; A_S = DEV = 2^64 gives 70.76004 (this filing, Appendix E.4).

heuristics.statement: All target-specific development computation of this package (and of the earlier versions in this lineage) is at most DEV = 2^60 target compressions; this includes the computation that selects the 256 A0 values (H6) and everything that is not in the counted preprocessing or the attack.
heuristics.scope: The allowance part of the ledger (with A_S, together 0.12% of T).
heuristics.extrapolation: Physical bound: the base runs used one 15-core machine for 14 days (1.8 x 10^7 CPU-seconds = 2^24.1; at the generous calibration of 2^21.383 units per CPU-second that is 2^45.5 units, 2^14.5 times below DEV, and even one full machine-year of all 15 cores is 2^50.2 units); the recorded runs (q3 studies, exhaustive passes, bucket measurements) are a small fraction of it. Selection of the A0 set (H6): the counts |R(A0)| are the cyclic cross-correlation over Z/2^32 of the histogram of F over the 9.9 x 10^9 valid pairs with the indicator of the 68,157,440 words w with s0(w + DW_8) - s0(w) = DS0_8, which one pass of the P5 kind (2^44.4 operations) plus a number-theoretic transform of length 2^32 (below 2^45 operations) computes: below 2^35 units, far inside DEV (and the exact sizes of the published set are recomputed in P5). The derivative work (Appendix C) used at most one 24-core machine and one RTX 3090 GPU for 30 days (below 2^55 units) plus less than 1 CPU-hour for the base filing's code/proof updates and selftests; the studies of Appendix E (this filing) used less than 10 CPU-hours of one laptop (below 2^37 units).
heuristics.limitations: A physical bound by wall-clock and core count, not a log of CPU time. The time spent by the author reading and writing is not computation in the cost model.

heuristics.statement: Let N be the number of successful variants on one chaining value (one group). The expected number of further successes seen from a success, sum_v Pr[A_v] E[N - 1 | A_v] / sum_v Pr[A_v], is at most delta = 1/25 (this filing; the base aed05522 used 0.564). This includes the premise that joint events of two variants on a real chaining value behave as on the uniform chaining values of the measured semi-free-start successes (H1 covers one variant at a time).
heuristics.scope: The group success bound Pr[N >= 1] >= S (1 - delta / 2) (Bonferroni, Section 6.4), hence N_G and the success bound. Not the validity of any output. With q3_model 2^-101.10: delta = 1/25 gives 70.73486; 1/50 gives 70.73011; 1/10 gives 70.74964; 0.564 (base) gives 70.89700; 1 gives 71.12764 (Appendix E.4).
heuristics.extrapolation: Structure: every success passes all of rows 16 and 17 (and 18) with W7 in F7, so pointwise N <= N17, the number of variants of the group that do; hence E[N - 1 | A_v] <= E[N17 - 1 | A_v] and delta <= delta17, the average over successes of the number of OTHER variants on the same chaining value that pass all of rows 16..17 with W7 in F7 (the base used N1, the 10-bit first row-17 test). Whole-group measurement (proof.md Appendix E.3, participant-run): for 2,500 verified successes, every row-16 entry of all 256 A0 buckets on the success's chaining value was enumerated exactly (all 32 words of G, all 768 A2, all preimages of phi(u) = s0(u) - u by a partitioned inverse over 2^32 u; validity tested; each entry evaluated from scratch through all 38 steps): 3,585,652 other entries (1434.3 per success, H1 expectation 1,428.8 plus near co-hits), 241,170 W7 passes, 48 with all of row 17, 0 reaching row 18, 0 further successes; every success was found in its own bucket. One-sided 99% Poisson limit of delta17: 0.02670 (delta = 1/25 is 1.50x it); of delta18: 0.00184. Near term separately on 31,875 successes: 391,103 near variants, 262,159 row-16 co-hits, 25,867 W7 passes, 545 with all of row 17, 0 reaching row 18 (rates equal to the base's near-term measurement). A further success would still need rows 18..37 (about 2^-57 given row 17).
heuristics.limitations: A premise. The measurements are participant-run; the successes are resampled SMC particles on uniform semi-free-start chaining values (clustered, not iid). The Poisson limit assumes independent observations; row-17 co-passes are clustered (dominated by near variants), so the true 99% bound on delta17 may exceed 0.02670 by an unknown factor; none of the 593 row-17-complete co-passes observed reached row 18. The transfer to real chaining values (first-block outputs) is supported only by H1's measurements of single-variant rates.

heuristics.statement: The 256 values A0_j of the set published by c99df2dc (qkniep) and 0ae69bcb (0xshikhar) are used as non-uniform advice (1 KiB). They are not claimed to be optimal; the cost of obtaining such a set is inside DEV (H4c); every quantity that depends on the set is recomputed here: the sizes |R_j| (exhaustively, 0 mismatches against the published sizes), SR = 191,773,672,732, and q3 (averaged over variants of this set in H2).
heuristics.scope: SR (hence N_G, the caps and the table sizes) and the variant sample of H2.
heuristics.extrapolation: The set matters: for a uniformly random A0 the mean size of R(A0) is 9,945,876,032 x 68,157,440 / 2^32 = 157.8 million, the set's mean is 749.1 million, a factor 4.75 (2.25 bits of attack cost). The maximum possible per-A0 count is 750,798,738 in the set. The selection is a correlation of two explicit objects (H4c) whose cost is below 2^35 units; even at the direct pair-by-pair cost, 2^33.2 pairs x 2^26.0 words x 3 operations = 2^60.8 operations = 2^49.4 units, together with the physical bound of H4c (2^45.5) it is 2^49.5, inside DEV = 2^60. The 256 values and sizes are listed in Appendix A.2; the file read by ledger38.py has these two columns.
heuristics.limitations: The set is advice from public filings and was not derived by us; the derivation cost is bounded, not executed.

heuristics.statement: The counted program is an honest program of the word RAM of collision-frontier-v5: every executed instruction of the classes add, sub, rsub, and, or, xor, shl, shr, ld, ldi, st, sti, li, rand, jmp costs 1, a conditional branch costs 2 (comparison and branch), one target compression costs 1 unit and the unit of every other operation is 1/C with C = 2728; constants (including 256-bit lane masks and per-lane constants) are instruction fields (immediates); the observers obs, mark, succ and halt are instrumentation of the interpreter and are not executed by the real program; scratch memory addresses are direct fields; at most 64 registers are live (43 are used).
heuristics.scope: Every operation count of the ledger (89, 75, 6, 43, 17, 3,142, 13, the preprocessing bodies of Appendix B.3 as executed by t_pre_d.py).
heuristics.extrapolation: The interpreter is in experiments/vt38.py (class Machine); the instruction classes are those of the model's primitive list; the per-body and per-path counts are executed counts, asserted by selftest item 4 and re-derived by t_cost.py, t_pre1.py and t_pre2.py (for this derivative's program and bodies: selftest item 4 and t_pre_d.py, Appendices C.4 and D.4); on 1,536 true buckets the machine's total operation count equals the reference model's (t_eq.py). Both the 0ae69bcb program and the earlier accepted r37 programs use 256-bit immediates and a branch price of 2 in the same way. Sensitivity: if every immediate operand of an ALU instruction, compare-branch or store were charged one extra operation, the base claim would be 71.10563 (+0.10 bit; proof.md Section 7, t_imm_d.py); not recomputed for this filing, where about the same +0.1 bit is expected.
heuristics.limitations: The organizer's reference note says "instruction constants require accounting in each submission"; our accounting is that an immediate is a field of an executed instruction that costs 1, and the sensitivity above charges one more operation for each immediate. No organizer ruling on immediates of 256 bits is cited. The four-lane vector trick relies on explicit lane arithmetic (bias 2^35), checked by the equivalence tests of Section 6.3.

restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is a verified collision of the target (Lemma 7, proof.md Section 5.4).

Construction: the two-block attack of ePrint 2026/1120 (38-step characteristic of its Table 3, two-bit conditions of Table 4, published semi-free-start pair of Table 5) with dense-part variants (A0, A1, A2) of the published dense part: the 256 A0 values of the public set (H6), the 768-value A2 list and every A1 for which the variant is valid (exact test). Lemma 3: every valid variant reproduces all A/E cells of rows -4..15 and every modular and s0 difference reaching rows >= 16. 2^37.48061 variants per chaining value. Row 16 by table: W16 = s0(Y + A1) - A1 + Z0 + c9(A2), (Y, Z0) depends on (CV1, A0) only (Lemma 5); row 16 holds iff W16 is in a set G of 32 words, and row 17 can hold for 22 of them (exact count); table T_j lists for each (Y, Z0) the variants of A0_j with W16 in these 22 words (at most 236,544 per bucket, 2 words per entry); each entry is then tested exactly: W7 in F7 (|F7| = 287,309,824) and rows 17..37 of both members.

Cost: fixed work caps. N_G = 106,837,024,868,983,061,305 groups (2^66.5340), each one first-block compression and 256 A0 blocks; caps on bucket entries, W7 passes, first-row-17-test passes and deep-path entries (Chebyshev, per-counter margins 2^-16, 2^-14, 2^-7, 2^-5), tested after every group with one group's overshoot charged. Counted program (experiments/vt38.py, unchanged from aed05522): prologue 89 operations + 1 unit, four blocks 75, 6 per entry, 43 per W7 pass, 17 per first-test pass, 3,142 per deep-path entry, epilogue 13; preprocessing as counted code (2^66.9387 units, tables zero-initialised and written, charged). Allowances A_C = 2^70 (H4a), A_S = 2^60 (H4b), DEV = 2^60 (H4c). Exact total 2^70.734858 (5359922159864254518422125/2728, ledgerx.py, proof.md Appendix E.4), claimed 70.73486.

Success probability at least 0.39 under H1 (one-trial uniform chaining value), H2 (q3 >= q3_model = 2^-101.10; six 99% Monte-Carlo bounds from two estimators, the lowest 2^-101.03905) and H5 (pair budget delta = 1/25, 1.50x the 99% Poisson limit of a whole-group row-17 measurement on 2,500 successes), by Bonferroni per group, independence of groups and Chebyshev for the caps: bound 0.39000000. No expected-work bound is used; the total cost is deterministic.

Memory (a reported metric): 2^80.42 bytes, dominated by the 256 tables (2-word bucket entries); the claim is a time bound in the track's word-RAM model with unit-cost table access (H3). baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.
